summary_md:
Revision 19 writes D154 and D158 into R4, R42, R54 and P15; every id, form and risk tag is kept.
R42: one rule for every operating-system error a save meets after its check, error named: not recorded, or not confirmed when its head record was published and not taken back.
R42 and P15: a writer refused once any part of its line is written reports not recorded, never nothing written; the part stays past the recorded entries as a torn entry (9c265a3).
R4 and R54: the table loaded as v1 is judged by its bytes before anything else, with what else breaks named after; a malformed rule value is named by rule, never a type error (7cb2e71, which still raises once at categorise.py:534).
One question: does R42's naming reach the six reads a save makes only to check (51c8b68 names nothing there and answers two with a conflict)?

questions.context: R42 (revision 19, D158) says every operating-system error a save meets after its check is reported with the error named: not recorded, or not confirmed when the save's head record was published and not taken back. R42 lists reading among a save's steps, so revision 19 counts the reads a save makes only to check something. At T12's 51c8b68 those reads turn the error into a value and name nothing. The append's comparison of the log's bytes (src/cma/case.py:1018) and a repair's re-check before its log rename (:921) read an unreadable log as changed and refuse with a conflict that asks the person to reload. The head record's re-check before its rename (:995) says the head file changed, and the read-back (:1067) says the log changed. A failed take-back (:1075) names no error, and a lock file that cannot be examined reads as removed or replaced (:795-799). 51c8b68 already maps the errors of the steps that change a file (D154). Under the default, T12 carries the error out of those six reads before its review. The alternative keeps R42's naming to the steps that change a file, and says that a re-check or read-back that cannot read answers as one that finds a change, naming no error.
options: Count the reads: every answer names the error, and a re-check that cannot read the log answers not recorded, never a conflict (design default; R42 as revision 19 writes it; T12 changes six answers before its review)

Name the error only at steps that change a file; a re-check or read-back that cannot read answers as one that finds a change, naming no error (R42 amended in the next revision; no build change at 51c8b68)

proposals.text: T03 (R4, revision 19): a v2 table with bank_code: true on a rule whose pattern is the list ['^UNPAID DD'] is refused naming that rule's pattern, never a TypeError (7cb2e71 raises where the codes the bank-code rules carry are gathered, src/cma/categorise.py:534); and a changed v1 that says frozen: false and carries such a rule is refused as a changed frozen table first.

T12 (R42, revision 19 default): inject a one-shot OSError into each read a save makes only to check (the byte comparison before the line, a repair's re-check, the head record's re-check, the read-back, the take-back, a lock file's examination) and assert the answer names the error and is not recorded or not confirmed, never a conflict; mark it invariants and name it p15.

T12 (R42): a head record's staging write fails while the head record cannot be read; the save answers not recorded, since no rename was made (51c8b68 answers not confirmed at src/cma/case.py:1060-1066).

When a test checks a refusal, assert what the caller is told (recorded, not recorded, not confirmed, nothing written) and the state left on disk, not only the exception's type: verify-76 failed T12 on a refusal whose type passed the old test (tests/test_case_log.py:1962) while its message said nothing was written over a torn entry.

R4, R42, R54 and P15 change; their ids, forms and risk tags do not. D154 kept the reach revision 18 gave R42's answer for a save the file system fails: every step the save takes after its check. R42 now states that answer as one rule (D158): every operating-system error a save meets after its check is reported, naming the error, as the save not recorded, unless the rename that publishes the save's head record was made and that head record was not then taken back, when the save is not confirmed. D158 says 'except where the head record was published'. R42 reads that as a head record that still lists the save's entry when the save answers, because a save whose read-back fails and whose take-back is made has taken back the head record it published, and R42 has called that save not recorded since revision 16. R42 also names the steps the rule covers. It counts among them the reads a save makes to re-check a case lock file, the log or the head record and to read the log back, because R42 lists reading among a save's steps and D158 says every step; at T12's 51c8b68 those reads still turn the error into an answer that names nothing, so revision 19 asks the owner whether that reach is meant. R42 and P15 now say that a writer refused once any part of its line is written, and before its head record is published, reports its save as not recorded, never as nothing written, and that the part written stays past the recorded entries as a torn entry, as a crash leaves it (D158, after verify-76, in which a lock lost after a short write was reported as nothing written while the next check named the incomplete entry). R4 and R54 now say that the table the system loads as v1 is judged by its bytes before anything else in it is checked: with any bytes but the pinned ones it is refused as a changed frozen table, naming the table, whatever it says of itself, and whatever else keeps it from loading is named after that (D158, after verify-77, which emptied v1's rules list and got 'no rules' instead of that refusal). R4 also says that a value the table format does not allow in a rule's field, such as a pattern given as a list, is a fault of that rule, named with the table's other faults and never raised as a type error (D158, after verify-77). D158 speaks of a malformed pattern value; R4 speaks of every rule field, as the design has for an id since revision 13, because T03's reviews since verify-65 have met the same type error for an id and for a pattern. requirements.md.old: A table that bears v1's id and calls itself frozen is that table only if its bytes match the hash the system pins in its own code (R54); with any other bytes, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it as a changed frozen table, naming the table, and SHALL use none of its rules. Every other table, whether or not it calls itself frozen, is checked rule by rule as the maintained lists are, and THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it, naming the rule, where a rule carries an exception (with frozen: true set on a copy of the v2 table whose cash rule's pattern is CASH DEPOSIT$, the refusal names the cash rule).
requirements.md.new: The table the system loads as v1 (R54) is that table only if its bytes match the hash the system pins in its own code, and THE SYSTEM SHALL compare them before it checks anything else in the table. With any other bytes, whatever the table says of itself, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it as a changed frozen table, naming the table, SHALL name after that whatever else keeps it from loading, and SHALL use none of its rules (with v1's rules list emptied, the refusal says first that v1 has been changed, and then that it has no rules). Every other table, whether or not it calls itself frozen or bears v1's id, is checked rule by rule as the maintained lists are, and THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it, naming the rule, where a rule carries an exception (with frozen: true set on a copy of the v2 table whose cash rule's pattern is CASH DEPOSIT$, the refusal names the cash rule). A value that the table format does not allow in a rule's field, such as a pattern given as a list, a mapping or a number, is a fault of that rule: THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the table naming the rule and the field, with the table's other faults, and SHALL NOT raise it as a type error (with the cash rule's pattern given as the list [CASH DEPOSIT] and unless: FPS on the same rule, the refusal names both of the cash rule's faults).

requirements.md.old: IF the file system fails a step that a save takes after its check (reading, writing, syncing, linking or renaming a file), THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL report the save as not recorded when the failure comes before the rename that publishes the save's head record, and as not confirmed when that rename was made and the head record cannot then be made durable because the folder that holds it cannot be synced; a save reported as not confirmed SHALL ask for the case log to be checked before anything else is saved. Either answer SHALL name the error, and THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT let the file system's error reach the save's caller as itself. Any part of the save's line already written stays past the recorded entries, as a crash leaves it. A read-back whose read fails is a read-back that fails, answered as above, and a failure during a take-back, in its rename or in the sync after it, answers not confirmed, as a take-back that is not made does.
requirements.md.new: IF the file system fails while a save is under way after its check, in a step the save takes (reading, writing, syncing, linking or renaming a file) or in a read it makes to re-check a case lock file, the log or the head record or to read the log back, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL report the save as not recorded, naming the error, unless the rename that publishes the save's head record was made and that head record was not then taken back, in which case THE SYSTEM SHALL report the save as not confirmed, naming the error, and SHALL ask for the case log to be checked before anything else is saved. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT let the file system's error reach the save's caller as itself. So a failure before that rename answers not recorded wherever it falls: at the empty head record written before the first entry's line, the log's opening, a write or sync of the line, the sync of the folder after a new log, a re-check, a repair's read of the log, its staging file, its log rename or the sync after it, or the head record's staging file or its rename. After that rename, a failure in the sync of the folder that holds the head record, which leaves the head record listing the save but not durable, answers not confirmed; a read-back whose read fails is a read-back that fails, taken back as above, and answers not recorded once its take-back is made; and a failure during a take-back, in its re-check, its rename or the sync after it, answers not confirmed, as a take-back that is not made does. Any part of the save's line already written stays past the recorded entries, as a crash leaves it.

design.md.new:
**What the owner decided on revision 18** (D154, D155, D158, 2026-11-20)
- D154 answered revision 18's question with its default: R42's answer for a save the file system fails reaches every step the save takes after its check. The owner built it in 51c8b68 (next section).
- D155 approved revision 18. D158: write D154 into R42, that every step of a save after its check reports an operating-system error as the save not recorded, naming the error, except where the head record was published (not confirmed); write into R42 and P15 that a lock lost after part of a line is written reports the save as not recorded, never nothing written, the part staying as a torn entry past the recorded entries (9c265a3); and write into R4 and R54 that a changed frozen v1 is refused as a changed frozen table before anything else is checked, with what else it breaks named after that, and that a malformed pattern value is named by rule, never raised as a type error (7cb2e71). Keep everything else in revision 18. Revision 19 writes all of it.
- Three readings. 'Except where the head record was published' is read as a head record that still lists the save's entry when the save answers: a save whose read-back fails and whose take-back is made has taken its head record back, and R42 has called it not recorded since revision 16. 'A malformed pattern value' is read for every rule field, as C1 has said for an id since revision 13. And 'every step' is read to take in the reads a save makes only to check, a re-check of a lock file, the log or the head record, and the read-back, since R42 lists reading among a save's steps. At 51c8b68 those reads still name no error, and revision 19 asks the owner whether that reach is meant (Options considered).

**What T12's twenty-sixth review showed** (verify-76; D156, D158, 2026-11-20)
- verify-76, T12's twenty-sixth review, judged the owner's 7c8fba2 against revision 18 and failed P15 on one major. With the case lock removed after a short write of the line, the re-check before the second write call raised the general refusal, 'a case lock file was removed or replaced while this window held the case; nothing was written', though part of the line was on disk past the recorded entries and the next check named it incomplete (src/cma/case.py:1010 there). The test for that schedule (tests/test_case_log.py:1962) checked the refusal's type and the bytes on disk, not what the save was told. Three minors recur: the producer claimed exit 0 with 'appending' for a held torn tail, where the contract test expects exit 4 and 'being saved'; the stress test does not force the interleaving claimed for it; and owner-only access was claimed for `cma case check`, which relies on the case root's permissions (R31) and checks no owner.
- The owner built 9c265a3 and then 51c8b68, neither yet reviewed; D156, the unblock, is pending. In 9c265a3 a refusal raised while the line is being written answers not recorded, saying that part of its entry was written, whenever the log is longer than the save's check found it (src/cma/case.py:1024-1035 at 51c8b68); a refusal before any byte of the line still says nothing was written. In 51c8b68 every operating-system error raised from an append's or a repair's steps after its check reaches the caller as the save not recorded, naming the error (_os_errors_as_not_recorded, :842-852, around _write at :880 and _replace_torn at :897), while _publish's own answer, not recorded or not confirmed, stands where the head record is published (:1056-1066). Tests mark both: a lock lost after part of the line (tests/test_case_log.py:2488), an operating-system error at the line, the first empty head record and a repair's rename (:2513), and the three tests that crashed a save with an OSError, now expecting not recorded (:52, :717 and :1715). The two new tests are marked invariants but not named p15.
- The major reads R42's 'a writer refused after its line ... SHALL report its save as not recorded' at its finest grain, for a writer refused partway through its line. D158 writes that into R42 and P15.
- Still open at 51c8b68:
  - The reads a save makes only to check something turn the file system's error into a value, so the answer names no error and sometimes gives the wrong cause. The append's comparison of the log's bytes with its check (:1018) and a repair's re-check before its log rename (:921) read an unreadable log as changed and refuse with a conflict that asks to reload. The head record's re-check before its rename (:995) says the head file changed. The read-back (:1067) says the log changed, and a take-back that fails (:1075) names no error. A lock file that cannot be examined is reported as removed or replaced (:795-799). R42 as revision 19 writes it asks each of these to name the error, and the conflicts to answer not recorded; revision 19 asks the owner (Options considered).
  - When a head record's staging write fails and the head record then reads as unreadable, or as another writer's under interference, _publish answers not confirmed (:1060-1066) though no rename was made; R42 asks for not recorded there, since the save made no rename.
  - A failed staging write or fsync of a head record or a repaired log still leaves its temporary file (:983-988, :924-929).
  - Fourteen tests added since review 20 are marked invariants but not named p15 (tests/test_case_log.py:2070-2513), which the project's gotcha asks for.
- The lesson is revision 18's, one call deeper: a refusal is an answer too, and it has to say what the save left behind.

**What T03's twenty-fifth review showed** (verify-77; D157, D158, 2026-11-20)
- verify-77, T03's twenty-fifth review, judged the owner's 9042fb4 against revision 18. It found that a table calling itself frozen under another id no longer skips the checks for well-formed rules, and failed R4 on two majors. First, the loader parsed and checked a table loaded as v1 before comparing its bytes with the pin, so a copy of v1 that kept id: v1 and frozen: true with its rules list emptied was refused for having no rules, not as a changed frozen table (src/cma/categorise.py:667 there). Second, a pattern given as a YAML list, on a rule that also carried unless: FPS, raised a TypeError from the bank-code membership test before either fault was named (:473 there). Three minors recur: README.md:78 still says a profile name can settle an ambiguous credit, the fifteenth review to find it; the producer claimed the rule-order shuffle for debits, which take the first matching rule by design (RENT PAYROLL); and the claim's compileall covers evals and tests, which the runner does not compile.
- The owner built 7cb2e71, not yet reviewed; D157, the unblock, is pending. load_ruleset works out whether a pinned table's bytes changed before it parses the table, and refuses a changed one as a changed frozen table first, adding 'It also fails to load' and the parse or rule fault when there is one (src/cma/categorise.py:676-691). _is_bank_code_text (:368-371) keeps a pattern that is not text from raising in the two bank-code checks (:440, :479), and the reserved-id check tests the id's type first (:451). Two tests mark it: a changed v1 refused as changed whatever else it breaks, with a key added, a malformed rule added or only a comment added (tests/test_rules_v2.py:1942), and a pattern given as a list, a mapping or a number named by rule beside the cash rule's unless (:1957).
- D158: write both into R4 and R54; revision 19 does that.
- Still open at 7cb2e71:
  - One path still raises a TypeError. The codes the bank-code rules carry are gathered by hashing each such rule's pattern (:534), so a v2 table with bank_code: true on a rule whose pattern is a list raises before any fault is named. R4 as revision 19 writes it rules that out, and the fix is the type test :440 already uses.
  - A changed v1 adds the parse or rule fault to its refusal only when that fault is a RulesetError (:682-688), so a changed v1 that says frozen: false and carries such a rule would raise the TypeError before the changed-table refusal.
  - README.md:78; RETURNED DD reversal linking, whose bank prefixes (:1020-1022) still hold UNPAID DD but not RETURNED DD; the reversal-linking time, which T22's timed recompute (R52) should include; and the exact candidates in the test at tests/test_rules_v2.py:1910.
- The lesson is verify-67's, finished: a validator that names faults has to survive every value the format can hold, or the fault it cannot name hides the ones it can.

The answer then names no error, and before the line it is a conflict that asks the person to reload (Context, T12's twenty-sixth review). (a) Count them among R42's steps: every answer names the error, and a re-check that cannot read what it checks answers not recorded, never a conflict; R42 says so since revision 19 (design default). (b) Keep R42's naming to the steps that change a file, and say in R42 that a re-check or a read-back that cannot read what it reads answers as one that finds a change: a conflict before the line, not recorded after it, and the take-back rules after the head record's rename, naming no error. *Chose (a)* as the default, because D158 says every step, R42 lists reading among a save's steps, and a person told to reload a case whose log cannot be read reloads into the same error. What (a) costs: T12 carries the error out of six reads before its review. (b) costs no build change and leaves a disk error answered as somebody else's save.
